bib.title: Fact, Fetch, and Reason: A Unified Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Fact, Fetch, and Reason: A Unified Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (FRAMES). Satyapriya Krishna, Kalpesh Krishna, Anhad Mohananey, Steven Schwarcz, Adam Stambler, Shyam Upadhyay, Manaal Faruqui (Harvard, Google DeepMind, Meta). arXiv:2409.12941v3 [cs.CL], 24 Jan 2025. Preprint (no venue printed).

COVERAGE: 46,725 of 46,725 chars read (all pages including limitations, future work and the prompt appendices). Nothing skipped. The references were skimmed. I did not open the target note: my grep for krishna/FRAMES in 11-retrieval-improvements.md returned nothing, so the note does not cite this paper yet. Figure 4 and Figure 3 data points are plots, so only text numbers are usable.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Multi-step retrieval lifts Gemini-1.5-Pro from 0.408 to 0.66 on FRAMES.
 number: 0.408 -> 0.66 (>50% relative); best setting (k,n,n_docs)=(5,5,10)
 setup: 824 multi-hop Wikipedia questions; Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514; BM25 over a Wikipedia dump; the model generates k queries per step for n steps, and only new docs are added to the context; planning prompt version; LLM autorater
 quote: "We achieved the best performance of 0.66 with the combination of (k, n, n_docs) = (5,5,10)" and "from an accuracy of 0.408 with single-step inference to 0.66 with multi-step retrievals."
 where: Abstract, Sec 1, Fig 4 caption (p.1, p.5-6)
2. Plain multi-step retrieval without planning instructions improves slowly and is costly. Query diversity is the bottleneck.
 number: ~0.45 -> ~0.52 at (5,5,2); six non-parallelizable inference calls
 setup: vanilla multi-step, no planning instructions, Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514
 quote: "accuracy increasing from ∼ 0.45 to ∼ 0.52 for the case of ( k, n, n_docs)=(5,5,2) for vanilla setting"; "which is computationally expensive since this requires six non-parallelizable inference calls (five for retrieval + one for final answering)"; "the lack of diversity in the queries generated by the model; it seemed like the model goes in the wrong direction in search retrievals and never corrects itself."
 where: Sec 3.2
3. Search-planning instructions (a few examples of an ideal query sequence, an instruction not to repeat queries, and "think step-by-step") bring multi-step accuracy near the oracle.
 number: 0.66 vs oracle 0.73
 setup: as in claim 1
 quote: "the model performance (0.66) through iterations reaches close to the oracle performance (0.73) by the end of five iterations of retrievals"
 where: Sec 3.2
4. Single-step BM25 retrieval helps only modestly, and recall in context is very low.
 number: 0.408 -> 0.452 (2 docs) -> 0.474 (4 docs); context recall 0.12 -> 0.15
 setup: Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514, top n_docs by BM25 from a Wikipedia dump added to the prompt. Gemini-Flash-1.5: 0.263 -> 0.288 -> 0.315.
 quote: "The model achieves an accuracy of 0.452 when the number of documents in the context is 2, and 0.474 when double the number of articles are added"; "increased from 0.12 (BM25-R(n_docs = 2) to 0.15 (BM25-R (n_docs = 4))"
 where: Table 3, Sec 3.1
5. Even with perfect retrieval (oracle docs) the model fails 27% of the time, mostly on reasoning, not retrieval.
 number: 0.729 oracle (Pro), 0.665 (Flash); ~80% of the oracle errors fall in numerical/tabular/post-processing
 setup: Oracle Prompt = question plus all gold Wikipedia articles
 quote: "Out of 27% samples where the model made errors, ∼80% of those misclassifications belong to numerical, tabular, and post-processing categories."
 where: Sec 3.1
6. Naive (no retrieval) accuracy across models.
 number: Pro 0.408, Flash 0.263, Gemma2-27b 0.308, Llama3.2-3B-I 0.115, Qwen2.5-3B-I 0.095
 quote: "Naive Prompt 0.408 0.263 0.308 0.115 0.095"
 where: Table 3. The small models have no retrieval rows because of context length.
7. BM25 retrieval helped most on the multiple-constraint and post-processing question types.
 number: ~8% and ~10%
 quote: "adding BM25 retrieved articles primarily helped with questions requiring reasoning through multiple constraints (∼8% improvement) and post-processing (∼10% improvement)"
 where: Sec 3.1, Fig 3a
8. In Fig 3b, multi-step search planning exceeds oracle performance on numerical reasoning (from the caption, no figure given in the text).
 quote: "Multi-step search planning increases performance for all reasoning types, with numerical reasoning surpassing oracle performance."
 where: Fig 3 caption
9. Dataset: 824 questions, each needing 2-15 Wikipedia articles.
 number: ~36% need 2 articles, ~35% need 3, ~16% need 4. Multiple constraints ~36% of questions, numerical ~20%.
 quote: "Approximately 36% of questions require two articles to answer, ∼35% require three articles, ∼16% require four"
 where: Sec 2
10. LLM-synthesised multi-hop questions were unreliable, so humans wrote the final set.
 number: >30% hallucinated; ~32% accuracy on the cleaned set; LLM struggled beyond four articles
 quote: "there was a high proportion of hallucinated questions and answers (>30%)"; "obtained an accuracy of ∼32%"
 where: Sec 2
11. LLM autorater agreed closely with humans.
 number: accuracy 0.96, Cohen's Kappa 0.889
 setup: Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514 as the grader on its own FRAMES answers
 quote: "accuracy: 0.96 and Cohen's Kappa: 0.889 for Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514 as autorating LLM"
 where: Sec 3.1
12. Data quality steps: 5.5% of samples were dropped on re-annotation after three months because the answer had changed. Yes/no questions were removed to prevent 50% guessing. Questions carry date anchors ("As of August 1, 2024").
 quote: "filtering out 5.5% of samples where the answer was no longer true after that period."
 where: Sec 2

LIMITS
- The authors concede possible pretraining contamination (Wikipedia is in training data) and that the dataset may not cover real-world query diversity.
- The retriever is BM25 only, over Wikipedia only, held fixed on purpose to isolate search planning. No dense or hybrid retriever, reranker or live web search was tested.
- Multi-step results were reported for Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514 only. Gemma, Llama and Qwen have no retrieval rows because their context windows are too short.
- No cost or latency numbers beyond "six non-parallelizable inference calls". No ablation separating the planning-prompt components: the examples, the no-repeat rule and the "think step-by-step" instruction were changed together.
- The 0.66 figure comes from Fig 4. The text gives no table of (k,n,n_docs) grid values.
- The models are May 2024 Gemini and Sep 2024 small models, so absolute numbers have dated.
- Future work listed: dense multi-hop retrievers (ColBERT, SimCSE), process supervision, distillation, context reduction, trained query generators.

BUILDS ON: Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Robertson et al. 1995 (BM25); Kojima et al. 2022 (zero-shot "think step-by-step"); benchmarks HotpotQA (Yang et al. 2018), MuSiQue (Trivedi et al. 2022), Multihop-RAG (Tang and Yang 2024), TruthfulQA, NaturalQuestions; FreshLLMs (Vu et al. 2023) and RealtimeQA (Kasai et al. 2024) for date anchoring; Yu et al. 2024 (RAG evaluation survey).

CODE: Algorithm 1 (Sec 3.2, p.4), the multi-step loop:
"C ← {Q}; for iteration i = 1 to n: for query j = 1 to k: generate search query Qij from context C; retrieve top n_docs Dij by BM25; C ← C ∪ (Dij \ C) {Add only new documents to context}; end; end; generate final response R using context C"
The auto-rater prompt (Fig 6) asks whether the ground-truth answer is present in the response and returns "Decision: TRUE/FALSE".

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.2) is an example question showing the factuality, retrieval and reasoning needs. Fig 2 shows the distribution of articles per question and of reasoning types. Fig 3a/3b (p.4) show accuracy by reasoning type for single-step and multi-step runs against the oracle. Fig 4 (p.5) is the accuracy curve over steps and queries, best 0.66 at (5,5,10), and is the one that shows the multi-step gain. Fig 5-7 are prompts: synthetic generation, auto-rating, and annotator instructions.

PROBLEMS: Table and figure text extracted cleanly. Fig 3 and Fig 4 data points are plot-only and were not read. No embedded instructions found. The reference list has duplicate entries (HotpotQA, TruthfulQA, the Yu survey) that are in the PDF itself.
